To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ROSAT All-Sky Survey (RASS) is a valuable source of data for studying the X-ray luminosity functions (XLF) and space density of AGN, but it is not a complete sample.

(a) The XLF of the AGN population is a power-law function with a slope of -1.4+/-0.1, and (b) the slope of the XLF of the galaxy population is -1.2+/-0.2, which is consistent with that found in other surveys.

the ROSAT Bright AGN sample has been shown to be dominated by AGN with X-ray luminosities of log L 44 erg/s and optical magnitudes of B < 17, and the XLF is consistent with a power law with slope -1.4, and a normalization of 0.0026 galaxies/Mpc3/deg2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the XLFs and X-ray properties of AGN, and their relationship to the properties of their host galaxies.
the X-ray emission from galaxies.
the study of galaxies and their evolution in the local Universe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the XLF of AGN is not well understood and that it is not clear whether it is dominated by AGNs or by star-forming galaxies.
the X-ray luminosity of AGN is dominated by the AGN component.
the X-ray emission of galaxies is dominated at all luminosities by the contribution of AGN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that the AGN XLF is not a simple extrapolation of the X-ray galaxy XLF and that the AGN fraction is a strong function of the host galaxy properties, especially its stellar mass, but also its star formation rate and the environment.
the AGN XLFs of the RBS and the 2XMM are consistent within the uncertainties.
the AGN XLFs of the two surveys are similar, but that the XLFs of galaxies in the RBS are different from that of galaxies in the 2RXS survey.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the X-ray luminosity functions of AGN and galaxies are very different.
the XLF of the AGN population is not well described by a single power-law.
XLFs of AGN in different environments (e.g. groups, clusters, field) are not the same.
